purpose: Characterize the pre-kernel server and stage target counterexamples. These cases are intentionally not registered in the MUnit, Isabelle-theory, or Python-e2e producer manifests and therefore verify or cover no plan claim.

execution.future_target: Run unchanged through ScriptedDataPlane and ConnectionKernel once checkpoints 2-8 provide those ports. Promote only then with explicit verifies/covers links.

cases.current_observation: Handler serves tools/list before initialize; it has no connection lifecycle state.
cases.target_counterexample: Fresh accepts only a standalone initialize request. This request must receive the phase-invalid Invalid Request response once the kernel owns lifecycle.
cases.evidence: mcp/src/mcp_server.scala: Handler.handle dispatches tools/list without a phase check

cases.current_observation: The line handler expects one object and has no JSON-RPC batch aggregation path.
cases.target_counterexample: MCP 2025-03-26 requires reception of this non-empty batch and one aggregate response containing the ping response; notification elements contribute no response.

cases.input: requests with numeric and string JSON-RPC ids, plus malformed JSON whose id is not recoverable
cases.current_observation: Handler echoes a parsed id directly in each response and uses null for parse errors, but does not carry a typed request identity through admission, terminal ownership, and shutdown.
cases.target_counterexample: The kernel preserves each valid string client request ID as the response correlation key regardless of completion order, rejects every numeric ID as InvalidRequest, and uses null only when JSON-RPC cannot determine a valid string id. This wire-ID rule is separate from T6's connection-owned completion token, which detects a second or unknown completion attempt.

cases.current_observation: The notification receives no reply but is otherwise ignored; no cancellation handle or late-result suppression exists.
cases.target_counterexample: If cancellation for an admitted valid string non-initialize request wins, cooperative work is cancelled, its slot is released once, and no response or late result escapes. A numeric cancellation target is ignored at the string-only boundary.
cases.evidence: mcp/src/mcp_server.scala: Handler.handle has no notifications/cancelled case

cases.input: more simultaneous tool requests than the future configured maxInFlight
cases.current_observation: serve forks one Isabelle thread for every non-blank input line; no direct-handoff admission bound or application queue policy exists.
cases.target_counterexample: Exactly maxInFlight ordinary requests are admitted. Each additional request receives an immediate structured overload error and creates no queued application work.

cases.input: three accepted requests whose completions occur in reverse order followed immediately by stdin EOF
cases.current_observation: The counter-based drain can finish before every worker publishes; the backend may stop with an admitted request lacking a terminal response.
cases.target_counterexample: EOF freezes admission, drains every completion that wins before one configured deadline, then cancels the rest before backend teardown. Every request has one recorded terminal disposition.
cases.evidence: mcp_test/src/mcp_handler_tests.scala: serve drains every dispatched reply before stopping on EOF

promotion_rule: A case may receive a producer registration or a plan verifies/covers link only after the named target behavior is implemented and the executable assertion is green. Pending, staged, and known-red cases are not coverage.
